topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: Antipodal Points
lecture_lines: Visualize a sphere in 3D space.
Identify points directly opposite each other.
These are called antipodal points.
Example: North and South Poles.
They share identical properties.
animations: Draw a 3D wireframe sphere in #FFFFFF, label it 'Sphere'.
Place two dots on opposite sides in #FF0000.
Label them 'Antipodal Points' in #FF0000.
Rotate the sphere to show North/South pole alignment.
Highlight the antipodal points with a glowing effect #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (Formalized)
lecture_lines: Continuous functions map spheres to Euclidean space.
At least one pair maps to one value.
This is the Borsuk-Ulam theorem.
Visualize a circle mapping to a line.
Opposite points land on the same spot.
animations: Draw a circle in #FFFFFF, label it 'Sphere'.
Highlight two points (antipodal) in #FF00FF.
Animate a smooth mapping function from circle to line.
Show two mapped points reaching same location #00FF00.
Apply bold color change to the antipodal point pair.

sections.title: The Stolen Necklace Problem
lecture_lines: Two thieves steal a necklace of beads.
Divide beads equally between both thieves.
Use the minimum number of cuts.
Borsuk-Ulam guarantees a fair division exists.
This is the Stolen Necklace problem.
animations: Display a circular necklace with two colors of beads.
Animate dividing the beads into two groups.
Illustrate making cuts using vertical lines #FFFF00.
Show groups moving to match values #00FFFF.
Display 'Fair Division Guaranteed' text in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Bridging Theory to Practice
lecture_lines: Necklace configuration space is a high-dimensional sphere.
Bead distribution represents continuous mapping.
Equal division is an intersection point.
animations: Display a hypersphere representing configuration space #FF00FF.
Animate a vector field flowing across the surface #FFFFFF.
Flash intersection points where division is fair #00FF00.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Topology solves complex discrete problems.
Existence proofs provide elegant solutions.
Topology is a tool for fairness.
